text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cfe245ae5f38188ac1bf7ebc9ee3a26 as of 2026-09-02T22:28:53.994Z: {"title":"Karen Rothe · Council · chal"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🗂️"} **Filled card. Not published. v2, re-verified 2 Sep 2026.** Karen Rothe · Council · challenger. Scored against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. **What v2 adds over v1:** the site's `sitemap.xml` gave real lastmod dates for every page, so no cell is dated "not published" any more · two policy pages missed on the first pass, **/priorities** (the canonical policy page) and **/why-im-running** (a fiscal diagnosis found nowhere else) · the launch article read in full rather than in summary · the platform has **four** named themes, not three · row 41 upgraded to Partial 1.0 · nomination status and the amalgamation ballot question added. ## Card
Field Value
Name Karen Rothe
Office Council
Kind chal (no 2022–26 City term — 2026 plan taken at face value, no record haircut)
Platform URL (2026) [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) (canonical policy page; site root [https://www.karenrothe.ca/](https://www.karenrothe.ca/) carries the same text)
Platform lastmod **2026-05-26** (sitemap.xml). Newest page anywhere on the site is 2026-05-27. **Nothing has been published in the 98 days since.**
Retrieved 2026-09-02
Scored answers (measures with an answer) **7 / 55**
Record lines 📋 (shown, not scored) 0 (no City office held 2022–26)
Letter (only at 5 scored answers: B+, B, C, D, or —) **—** · awaiting Joa's click. Internal proposal at the bottom of this page.
Checked by · date Verifier · 2026-09-02 (v2, full-site sweep)
### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **—** She names the fiscal problem and publishes no answer to it: "We have expensive capital projects; we have an aging population; we have a large deficit; we have an affordability issue." No tax rate, no cap, no formula, no class-ratio position anywhere on the site or in launch coverage. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running](https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
Downtown order M26 / M27 **—** Her downtown text is about access and vibrancy, not order: "I want to remove the barriers stopping people from coming downtown and restore the vibrant downtown that has been lost." No enforcement, bylaw-hours, encampment or unified-command position published. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **—** No housing volume, composition, tenure or land position on any of the twelve pages. The nearest thing to a housing sentence runs the other way: "there is constant construction and disruption," named as one of six problems. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running](https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater, the CRD and the combined household number appear nowhere. "Affordability" is named as an issue four times and never costed. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running](https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
Written program — **yes** Written, authorized, four named themes on a dedicated /priorities page: "Creating Trust Through Better Leadership", "Restoring Downtown, Protecting Our Neighbourhoods", "Better Planning for Better Outcomes", "Responsible Stewardship". No targets, no costings, no instruments, no dates, and no line changed since 26 May 2026. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
### Source ledger (what was read, when it was last touched)
Source lastmod retrieved What it carries
[/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) 2026-05-26 2026-09-02 **Canonical policy page.** Four themes. Carries rows 14, 18, 41, 42, 50, 51, 53.
[/why-im-running](https://www.karenrothe.ca/why-im-running) 2026-05-26 2026-09-02 Fiscal and demographic diagnosis found nowhere else. Six named problems, no instrument. Carries no mark; sharpens four doors.
[site root](https://www.karenrothe.ca/) 2026-05-26 2026-09-02 Duplicates /priorities (with one typo, "leave the the bill"). Quotes taken from /priorities.
[/about-karen](https://www.karenrothe.ca/about-karen) 2026-05-26 2026-09-02 Biography only. Background, which is not a source.
[/updates](https://www.karenrothe.ca/updates) 2026-05-26 2026-09-02 "No updates posted yet."
[/our-events](https://www.karenrothe.ca/our-events) 2026-05-22 2026-09-02 No events posted.
/donate · /volunteer · /contact-karen · /get-updates · /request-a-lawn-sign · /privacy-policy 2026-05-27 2026-09-02 Operational only. Karen Rothe is her own financial agent. Signs from 19 Sep 2026.
[Victoria News launch article](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/27/a-city-where-families-can-thrive-vic-west-resident-to-run-for-council/) 2026-05-27 2026-09-02 Read in full. Intent announced 21 May, candidacy 27 May. Five direct quotes, none carrying an instrument.
[City of Victoria elections](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/elections) — 2026-09-02 Accepted nominations so far: Alto, Atkinson (Mayor), Gardiner (Council). **Rothe not yet filed.** Close 11 Sep 4 PM.
## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date** = lastmod, retrieved. Read a row across and it is the one-line cell format. A dash is unknown, not a fail. Mentions do not resolve up to Agrees. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition — Nothing on supply, composition, missing middle, 3-bedroom share, below-market or rental share across all twelve pages and the launch article. **Flagged tension:** she names "constant construction and disruption" as one of six problems, which sits against a 12,000-home target. Not opposition — she never addresses the target — but the first thing to put to her. — —
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — City land, land bank and co-ops appear in no published text. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening — No permit-time position. No standard, category, or number. — —
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs and expedited streams do not appear. Her stated interest in "art and building design" is background, not a source. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty — No vacancy target, no DCC position, no suite amnesty. — —
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — Nothing on unified command, co-location or a downtown operations desk. Her one downtown sentence is scored once, on row 18. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — Crisis response and the right-responder question do not appear. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours position. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — "Perspectives and feelings matter and they need to be backed up by facts and data" is about how council decides, not about enforcement targeting. Carried as context on row 42; the leap to hotspot data would be adjacency. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws — Sheltering bylaws do not appear. — —
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — Buffer zones and child-focused spaces do not appear. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting — Encampments, removal protocol and lighting do not appear. — —
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) — Names the problem, publishes no answer: "We have expensive capital projects; we have an aging population; we have a large deficit; we have an affordability issue." Raising a topic with no goal and no instrument is a Mention, and Mentions do not resolve up. No rate, no cap, no formula, no class-ratio position. — —
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule **Partial 1.0** "The tendency is to kick the can down the road and leave the bill for others to pay later. I won't do that." · Commits against intergenerational deferral, the argument M66c is built on, with nothing behind it: no debt rule, no supermajority override, no published debt set, nothing on the over-collection refund. Context: "I know how much pain and financial hardship can be avoided by planning ahead," and "We have a hard time seeing and paying for something that will happen in the future, even if it's a certainty." [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
15 M66d the Household Bill — The combined household number, water, sewer, stormwater and the CRD appear nowhere. "Affordability" is named four times across two pages and never carries a figure. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger — No downloading position, no ledger, no refusal threshold. Notable given her stated provincial career, but background is not a source. — —
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — The CRD, regional water rates and the filtration plant do not appear. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Partial 1.0** "I want to remove the barriers stopping people from coming downtown and restore the vibrant downtown that has been lost." · Commits to a downtown outcome with no instrument and no number: no vacancy target, no lever named, no mandate, no flagship event, no economic plan. Which barriers is never stated. Context: "Without people in the economic and cultural heart of the city, we don't have a downtown"; "we have businesses that are leaving the City"; and at launch, "When local businesses are healthy, people have jobs." [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — "We have expensive capital projects" names the cost, not the approval instrument. A Mention, so a dash. Parking and permit fees do not appear at all. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — Nothing on government-to-government tables, Indigenous procurement, lək̓ʷəŋən place names, cultural protocols or an urban Indigenous liaison, on any page or in launch coverage. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) — Demoviction, short-term rentals and indoor heat do not appear. — —
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — Housing allocation and waitlists do not appear. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput — Homelessness is addressed nowhere: not on the four content pages, not in the launch article. On a flagship measure, that is the loudest silence on the card. — —
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) — "Victoria should be a city where families can thrive; where young people can see a future, where seniors feel safe and connected, where businesses can succeed, and where neighbourhoods feel welcoming, vibrant, and cared for" raises families, youth and seniors with no goal state and no instrument. A Mention, so a dash in every column. Childcare spaces, family doctors and the 18–25 cohort are not addressed. — —
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — Schools and SD61 do not appear. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm — Graffiti, pests, sanitation hours and public art do not appear. "neighbourhoods feel welcoming, vibrant, and cared for" is tone, and tone is not a source. — —
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) — No corridor, signal, intersection, school-zone or safety-audit position. "transportation" appears only inside lists of core responsibilities. Mention, so a dash. — —
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls — Two near-misses, both Mentions: "efficient public transportation matters" (/why-im-running) and, inside the sentence scored on row 41, "public transportation systems that work for all". Neither names a goal state the City controls, and one sentence cannot carry a second mark. Walking, sidewalks and crossings appear nowhere. — —
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms — Accessibility audits and public washrooms do not appear. "we have an aging population" is a Mention, and the leap to an accessibility programme would be adjacency. — —
30 M25 fix roads first — "Infrastructure matters" and "We need to prioritize what matters most and manage those priorities" are generic prioritisation. No maintenance backlog, no pothole standard, no build-versus-repair sequencing rule. Mentions, so a dash. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — Business security costs do not appear. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — Paramedicine and call-volume reduction do not appear. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) — VicPD, Esquimalt, the funding dispute and a regional review appear nowhere. "public safety matters" and "They're worried about safety" are Mentions, and Mentions do not resolve up. — —
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting and the surveillance limit do not appear. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — No dashboard, no enforcement record, no crime number. "As our provincial capital, we should be setting the standard for what a safe, livable, welcoming city looks like" is aspiration without a goal state, and frame is not a source. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues — Heritage standards, street furniture and cultural venues do not appear. — —
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project — Her Centennial Square sentence is scored once, on row 50, as a process statement. Read in full context it objects to that plan and that timing, not to renewal, so it is **not** an Opposed mark here. Pedestrianisation and a signature project are not addressed. — —
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks — Waterfront walkways, ornamental lighting and parks do not appear. — —
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor — "the economic and cultural heart of the city" describes downtown. No arts, sport, venue or funding-floor position. — —
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — Competitive testing of waste collection or street cleaning does not appear. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews **Partial 1.0** "I will be a responsible steward of our limited resources and will focus on the core responsibilities of local government: infrastructure, transportation, public safety, affordability, and public transportation systems that work for all." · Commits — "I will be", "will focus on" — to M65's jurisdiction test, is this the City's job, with no instrument: no zero-based cycle, no \$50K grant threshold, no three-part test, no savings figure. On /priorities this is its own theme, "Responsible Stewardship". **Upgraded from Weak 0.5 in v1** under ambiguity-resolves-upward: a stated "I will" is Commits, not Agrees. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard **Weak 0.5** "Council has delegated its responsibilities to staff. This has created a lack of transparency, a lack of accountability, and an erosion of public trust." · Agrees with the goal M67 exists to serve — residents able to hold council to account between elections — with no instrument: no dashboard, no KPI set, no cadence. Context: "Perspectives and feelings matter and they need to be backed up by facts and data," and "We need to make decisions today that are informed by experience and data." [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — City real-estate holdings do not appear. Twenty-two years as a strata property-management coordinator is background, and background is not a source. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — GIS, consultation imagery and LIDAR do not appear. Reading "informed by experience and data" onto a GIS programme would be adjacency. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — Municipal use of AI does not appear. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement, open data, Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic — Climate targets, district energy and seismic or coastal resilience appear nowhere. **Closest near-miss on the card:** "The last decade has taught us that things will change and that we need to be prepared for those changes, many of which are a certainty." In context that paragraph is about paying for future costs, not about hazard, so scoring it on M64b would be adjacency. One clarifying sentence from her turns this into a mark. — —
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness — No published position on trees, mode share, ecosystems or emergency preparedness. Her career work on the 2017 Williams Lake evacuation and BC Search and Rescue funding is background, which the rules exclude. This is the largest gap on the card between what she plausibly knows and what she has written down. — —
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule **Weak 0.5** "It shouldn't have taken a public outcry to stop the redevelopment of Centennial Square; a council that listens and is engaged would have quickly realized it wasn't the right plan nor the right time." · Agrees with M78 step 1, consultation before commitment, as a goal. A commitment to listen is not a named process: no 5-step sequence, no \$25M threshold, no material-change rule, and the sentence describes what a council would have done, not what she will do. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response **Partial 1.0** "I commit to listening, communicating, and ensuring as much transparency as possible." · Commits, with no instrument: no Integrity Commissioner, no MNP implementation tracker, no 60-day response standard, no draft-before-adoption rule. "as much transparency as possible" is a discretionary standard, not a service standard. Context: her diagnosis that council has delegated its responsibilities to staff is the council-staff boundary problem the MNP report addresses. [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration — Lobbyist registry, FOI fees, mandate letters and council pay do not appear. — —
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans **Weak 0.5** "Community associations have long been stewards of these neighbourhoods, and their hard-won experience is critical to the long-term health of our communities." · Agrees that neighbourhood associations should carry weight, with no instrument: no grant line, no delivery-partner role, no Local Area Plan programme, no schedule, nothing on language access. Context: "Victoria is a city of neighbourhoods." [https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities](https://www.karenrothe.ca/priorities) lastmod 2026-05-26, retrieved 2026-09-02
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — Annual surveys, turnout and ballot access do not appear. Near-miss: "Victoria needs practical leadership, clear communication, and decisions that are informed by the people who live, work, build, serve, and invest in this city." That is the same value already carried on rows 50 and 51; giving it a third cell would be thin-slicing one theme across three measures. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) — No position. **This dash is now material:** the 17 Oct ballot carries a non-binding Saanich-Victoria amalgamation question, so every candidate will be asked. Silence here will not survive to election day. — —
## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **v2 revision log (2 Sep 2026).** Found and read two policy pages missed in v1 — **/priorities** and **/why-im-running** — via `sitemap.xml`, which also supplied real lastmod dates for all twelve pages. Re-read the launch article in full rather than in summary. Net effect: **no new scored cells**, one upgrade (row 41, Weak 0.5 → Partial 1.0), sharper evidence on 14 dash rows, all four open doors better documented, and three new facts below. n unchanged at 7; mean 0.71 → 0.79; band unchanged. - **Full source inventory, all twelve site pages read.** /priorities · /why-im-running · site root · /about-karen · /updates ("No updates posted yet") · /our-events (none posted) · /donate · /volunteer · /contact-karen · /get-updates · /request-a-lawn-sign · /privacy-policy. Plus the Victoria News launch article in full and the City of Victoria elections page. - **Searched and not found:** any campaign Facebook, Instagram, X, Bluesky, Threads, TikTok, YouTube or LinkedIn account · any completed candidate questionnaire · any all-candidates forum or debate · any second news interview · any endorsement · any mention on the Victoria West Community Association site. The only Wayback capture of the site is 28 May 2026. Absence is recorded as absence, not as a fail. - **The campaign has published nothing since 27 May 2026.** Every page's lastmod falls between 22 and 27 May; the updates and events pages are still empty 98 days later. Lawn signs are advertised for 19 Sep. Whatever else the card says, this is a campaign that has not moved in public since launch week, six weeks out from the vote. - **She has not filed.** As of 2 Sep 2026 the City lists accepted nominations for Alto and Atkinson (Mayor) and Gardiner (Council). Rothe is declared, not nominated. Nominations close **11 Sep at 4 PM**. Her column is provisional until then. - **The ballot carries a Saanich-Victoria amalgamation question** (non-binding, 17 Oct). Row 55 is therefore a live gap, not a technicality. - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Seven sentences carry the seven scored cells, each used once, all from /priorities: (1) "kick the can down the road… I won't do that" → row 14. (2) "remove the barriers stopping people from coming downtown" → row 18. (3) "I will be a responsible steward… core responsibilities of local government" → row 41. (4) "Council has delegated its responsibilities to staff…" → row 42. (5) Centennial Square / "a council that listens and is engaged" → row 50. (6) "I commit to listening, communicating, and ensuring as much transparency as possible" → row 51. (7) "Community associations have long been stewards…" → row 53. - **Where the Mentions rule did the most work.** Six cells were held at a dash that a looser reading would have opened: row 13 (large deficit), row 19 (expensive capital projects), row 28 (efficient public transportation matters), row 30 (infrastructure matters), row 33 (public safety matters), row 35 (should be setting the standard for a safe city). Each raises a topic without a goal state or an instrument. Opening them would have added six Weak 0.5 marks, lifted n to 13 and pulled the mean **down** to 0.65 — still D. The letter does not depend on this call, but the coverage number does. - **Contested allocations, recorded so they can be re-argued.** Row 41 versus row 28: the "core responsibilities" sentence names both a jurisdiction test and public transit. It sits on row 41 because "core responsibilities of local government" is M65's own test nearly word for word, and because M23b's central point is that transit is *not* a municipal decision. Row 18 versus row 27: "remove the barriers stopping people from coming downtown" could be traffic (M19) rather than downtown revival (M71); she never says which barriers, and M71 is the closest whole. - **Actions found that contradict a 2026 sentence (measure, vote, source):** none. No City office held 2022–26, so no record to weigh, no 📋 line, no incumbent cap. Challenger rule applied: 2026 plan at face value, no haircut for having no record. - **The Centennial Square line stays withdrawn as a divergence.** Her objection is to that plan and that timing, not to renewal, and M45c's own mechanism — consult, visualize, shortlist, referendum — is what she asks for. Scored once, on row 50, as agreement with process. A snippet is not a source, and it cuts both ways. - **Background excluded, deliberately.** The 2017 Williams Lake evacuation, BC Search and Rescue funding, the Metro Vancouver regional growth strategy and 22 years of strata property management are professional background. Background is not a source. This costs her rows 16, 44, 48 and 49, where she may be the strongest candidate in the field and has published nothing to prove it. - **Flagged tension, not a divergence.** "there is constant construction and disruption" is named as one of six problems. The Program's housing, road, pedestrianisation and signature-project measures all increase construction. She never addresses a housing target, so this is not Opposed — but it is the question most likely to turn into one. - **Rows to put to the candidate before publication:** row 1 (does "constant construction and disruption" mean fewer homes, or better-sequenced ones?) · row 13 (a large deficit and an affordability issue — what happens to the residential rate?) · row 14 (does "I won't do that" extend to a written debt rule?) · row 18 (which barriers?) · row 48 (does "prepared for changes that are a certainty" include seismic and coastal?) · row 55 (how will she vote on amalgamation?). - **What would move this card fastest:** one costed fiscal section with a tax-rate position (rows 13–15), one housing paragraph containing a number (rows 1–5), one sentence on downtown order distinct from downtown vibrancy (rows 6–8), and one sentence turning her emergency-management career into a written commitment (rows 48–49). Four additions, three doors opened, and the card moves out of D. - **Next mandatory re-check:** **11 Sep 2026** at nomination close — confirm she filed, and confirm the column. Then on any site change; the sitemap gives reliable lastmod values, so a weekly check of `karenrothe.ca/sitemap.xml` is enough to detect a platform release without re-reading the site. - M83 (civic access / public correction, \$0) has no cell in this 55. Not scored. ## INTERNAL proposed letter — not the live letter **PROPOSE: D** · n = 7 · mean 0.79 Sum of scored marks: 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5 = **5.5** across **7** scored cells (rows 14, 18, 41, 51 at Partial 1.0; rows 42, 50, 53 at Weak 0.5). Mean **0.786**, inside the **D** band (0.50–0.99). D is already one of the five live letters, so no mapping is needed. **Unchanged from v1** despite the fuller evidence base: the extra reading raised the mean from 0.71 to 0.79 and did not cross a band. **This is a proposal, not the live letter.** The card above shows **—**. The live letter waits for Joa's click and compute must not overwrite it. **What the proposal measures.** Not hostility to the Program — she is not Opposed on a single cell of 55 — but distance from it. Four Partials and three Weaks, and every one of the seven is a goal without an instrument. Forty-eight dashes because she has not spoken to those measures, not because she failed them. After a full-site sweep the shape did not change, which is itself the finding: a four-theme values platform, no numbers anywhere, unchanged since launch week. **Fragility.** At n = 7 the letter is thin, and it is thin in a specific direction. Four Partial-plus marks on a detailed release carry the mean to 1.05, into C−, which maps to **C** on the live set. The band is roughly one costed section away. Hold at **—** through 11 Sep: if she files with a fuller platform the card changes materially, and if she files with this one, D is well evidenced.
